name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after 20% gas cuts to plants; Gulf fertiliser exports down about 70% on Hormuz
state: Egyptian granular urea was about $535 a tonne FOB for November, up about 17% from roughly $457 in September, after gas supplies to plants were cut by 20% from 1 Nov (Fertilizer Daily, 9 Nov). Middle East fertiliser exports fell about 70% in September from a year earlier as Hormuz stays largely closed, according to Kpler (The National, 31 Oct). Gulf shipments continue at reduced volumes and searches on 16 Nov found no 60% three-month rise in urea, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring face higher input costs; analysts link tight supply to smaller harvests and food inflation in 2027.
rubric_hit: Watch: Gulf exports disrupted by Hormuz restrictions; urea rise below 60% in three months

sources.title: Fertilizer Daily — Egyptian urea at USD 535 a ton as gas cuts hit plants
The National — Middle East fertiliser exports decline by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
